clue.text: Turner, ascendant artist, seasoned like wine or cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue something ascendant rises, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
wine and cheese that have been aged and seasoned are called mature

explanation.surface: A remark that the painter Turner, rising in reputation, has aged well like a vintage or a cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter J. M. W. Turner, but it is the definition: the armature is the part of a motor that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: In an electric motor or generator the armature is the rotating component, so it is literally a thing that turns.

clue.text: Wine too old, unlimited

indicators.note: without limits means the outermost letter at each end of the phrase is removed

parts.note: someone past it is too old to do the job

explanation.surface: A complaint that a bottle has been kept far too long and has gone beyond its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips the first and last letters, P and T, from PAST IT. ASTI is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is an Italian sparkling white wine, so it is an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Wine, less than half its content given up for soak

indicators.note: in a down clue, something given up is pushed upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
only the first three of the seven letters survive, fewer than half of the word

parts.note: the wine's content here is its alcohol
to ret flax or hemp is to soak it so the fibres separate

explanation.surface: A wine has lost much of its alcohol, perhaps for a drinker who soaks it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half' keeps ALC from ALCOHOL; 'given up' turns it to CLA. 'Soak' looks like a drunkard but is the verb RET, used of flax. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the traditional British name for red Bordeaux wine, so it is one kind of wine.

clue.text: Wine from another world sadly unfinished

parts.note: Mars is another planet, a world other than ours

indicators.note: the word is left without its final letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: A lament over a wine imported from some other planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final S of ALAS, leaving ALA. Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Wild cormorant abandons north for roadrunner?

indicators.note: wild suggests unruly disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the cormorant leaves behind a letter, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A seabird gone feral flies south instead of north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes N from CORMORANT to leave CORMORAT, and 'Wild' rearranges those letters. The question mark warns that 'roadrunner' is not the desert bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is something that runs along the road, so the bird's name is read playfully as a description.

clue.text: Wine, food and beer

parts.note: pies are a kind of food
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A pub menu offering wine, something to eat and a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Piesporter is a Riesling from the Mosel village of Piesport in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Piesporter is a German white wine from Piesport on the Mosel, so it is one particular wine.

clue.text: Wine vault's contents

definitions.meaning: A red or white wine from the Bordeaux region of France
a burial vault holds the places where the dead lie

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine laid down in a cellar vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' suggests a wine cellar, but the second sense is a burial vault and what lies in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux appellation, and burial places are what a funeral vault contains.

clue.text: Two cups and their false contents no con — small size becomes capital

parts.note: a bra has two cups

indicators.note: one size turns into another, the larger letter replaced by a smaller one
no con means those letters are dropped

parts.note: silicone implants are what false cups may be filled with
taken as written
A is the smallest bra cup size

explanation.surface: A bra and its padding with no deception: going down a size turns into a major event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes CON from SILICONE, leaving SILIE; 'becomes' turns its E, a bigger cup size, into A, the small size. Brasilia is the capital of Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the capital city of Brazil, a planned city built in the 1950s.

clue.text: Willow more blooming when polled

indicators.note: polled means having the head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: rosier means more rosy, more blooming in complexion

explanation.surface: A willow tree looks healthier once its top is pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polled', like a pollarded tree, removes the head, the R of ROSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Somalian's country

indicators.note: the possessive here reads as has, so the word holds the country inside it

explanation.surface: A question of which nation a Somali citizen belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somalian' leads to Somalia, but the African country is held inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa, so it is a nation by name.

clue.text: Shift proves simple initially, in E sharp

indicators.note: to shift things is to move them around, so the letters change places
initially takes just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A musician demonstrates that shifting to E sharp is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' rearranges PROVES with S (first of 'simple'), IN and E. 'E sharp' looks like a musical note, but 'sharp' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, quick-witted person reacts readily, which is the sense of being quick to respond.

clue.text: Wine, given a little time on song? One put away

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: music is what a song is made of
I is the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A drink while a short spell is spent singing, before the singer is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song' is the music it is made of, and 'One' is the Roman numeral. Muscat is a sweet wine made from the grape of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a sweet wine made from the muscat grape, an example of the category.

clue.text: Wine vault metal

parts.note: a vault is an arched chamber
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Wine stored in a vault, perhaps in metal containers.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambertin is a grand cru red Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin, so it is a particular wine.

clue.text: Even parts of clue contain how to enter this sport

indicators.note: the two letters go round the other piece
the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, are taken from the word

parts.note: this answer is written into the grid from left to right, in the across direction

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to take up a sport, hidden in the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even parts of' takes L and E from 'clue'. The self-reference is literal: this is an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Port wine's last to partake of, about right by lake

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the only one taken
the verb goes round the other letter

parts.note: to have food or drink is to partake of it

explanation.surface: Port, the last of the wine, to be enjoyed by a lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a harbour town. 'about' puts R inside HAVE. Le Havre is a French port on the Seine estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport in Normandy, northern France, so it is a port city.

clue.text: Wine and cheese topped with drink

indicators.note: topped means having the top cut off; in a down clue the first letter goes

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a sling is a cocktail, as in a gin sling

explanation.surface: A wine-and-cheese evening with a cocktail on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' looks like 'with a topping', but it beheads BRIE. Riesling is a white wine grape and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine made from the grape of that name, so it is one sort of wine.

clue.text: Keep object cold in place of pole

indicators.note: one letter stands where another was

parts.note: to object is to protest
S is the south pole
C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: A request to keep something chilled rather than at the Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun but is the verb PROTEST; 'in place of' puts C where its S was.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something safe is to guard or shield it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Star lacking core providing speed

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a star is a famous person, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity without depth who can only offer swiftness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking core' removes B, the middle letter of nine-letter CELEBRITY. 'Star' is a famous person, not a heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pudding stuffed with heart of poultry given very loud abuse

indicators.note: the pudding has something pushed inside it

parts.note: sago is a starchy milk pudding

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter of the word

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A dessert stuffed with chicken served with a loud row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes L, the middle letter of seven-letter 'poultry'. SLAG OFF is British slang for criticising someone harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag someone off is British slang for insulting them, so it means to abuse verbally.

clue.text: Brainless dolly should lose some weight

definitions.meaning: a dim, foolish person, the slang sense of the word
a short bar with weights at each end used for exercise

explanation.surface: A dim young woman ought to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should lose' is link, and also hints that the weight is used in a gym to lose weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a stupid person and also names a hand weight lifted in exercise.

clue.text: Result, given lob?

definitions.meaning: the outcome or final consequence of something
a lob is a ball hit high, a shot sent upwards

explanation.surface: What came of a high shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the playful reading: a lob is a shot that goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome of events is its result, and a lobbed ball is literally a shot hit up.

clue.text: Wine, a degree sweet

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
Rolo is a brand of chocolate-covered toffee sweets

explanation.surface: A wine that is somewhat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a degree' looks like 'slightly', but it is BA; ROLO is a British chocolate brand. Barolo is an Italian red from Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Barolo is a red Italian wine from Piedmont made from Nebbiolo grapes.

clue.text: Wine and places to buy it on account

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: wine can be bought in bars

explanation.surface: Wine and the bars that sell it on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: Barsac is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet dessert wine from the Bordeaux region, a particular wine.

clue.text: Endless bad mood admitted by Al Gore, given corruption — he should have seen it coming

definitions.text: he should have seen it coming

indicators.note: the letters let the other piece in among them
corruption means the name's letters are spoilt and rearranged
the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a strop is a fit of sulky bad temper

explanation.surface: Al Gore, sulking and corrupted, ought to have predicted his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the former US vice-president's name splits around the trimmed sulk: A at the front, LOGER after. The definition is the joke: a stargazer ought to have foreseen it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stargazer who claims to foretell the future would be expected to foresee events.

clue.text: Audibly audible elephants, perhaps

indicators.note: audibly signals that a word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: something audible can be heard

explanation.surface: Elephants making noise that is clearly heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks elephants as an example of animals in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants travel in a herd, so a group of them is an example of one.

clue.text: Wine to show a bit of leg

definitions.meaning: a white wine from the Rhine region of Germany
the joint in an animal's hind leg

explanation.surface: Wine that makes someone flash a little leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show' is link. HOCK is the British name for German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the British term for German white wine and also an animal's ankle joint.

clue.text: Bulb working with something charged

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A light bulb that is switched on and charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a lamp, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is the edible bulb of a plant of the lily family.

clue.text: Wine not entirely feeble, leave for storage

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside, as a store does
the word is cut short by a letter at its end

parts.note: frail means weak or feeble
scat is a command to leave at once

explanation.surface: A weak wine should be put away in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' is the curt command to go away, not a holiday. Frascati is a dry white wine from the hills near Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Frascati is a dry white wine from the hills near Rome, an example of a wine.
